newsitem.title: CANADA: ATHLETICS-BAILEY UNHAPPY WITH SPRINT CONDITIONS, RIPS ORGANIZERS.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-BAILEY UNHAPPY WITH SPRINT CONDITIONS, RIPS ORGANIZERS.

text.p: Olympic champion Donovan Bailey was upset with race conditions in the hours just before Sunday's 150-meter, $1-million match sprint against Michael Johnson, saying he would compete under "mental duress."

Reigning world and Olympic 100-meter champion Bailey accused race organisers of "deceitfulness" but was prepared to go ahead with the 150-meter race against Olympic 200 and 400 meter champion Johnson with a $1 million prize to the winner.
Just three hours before the race was scheduled to start, Bailey issued a statement in which he criticised race organisers and Mondo, the manufacturers of the track surface.
"I would like to express to my fans, to Canada, and to the world-wide media, that I run today under mental duress," Bailey's statement began.

"In February, my manager Ray Flynn received a fax from Mondo Sports which contained exact dimensions along with a scaled drawing of a track that I agreed to run on as part of the event today in the SkyDome.

"I arrived at SkyDome Friday evening, May 30, to inspect the track. The track in SkyDome is completely different from the track which I visualized in my training over and over every day since my training began for this race."
The statement did not go into specifics about Bailey's objections to the Mondo track -- a specially-designed two-lane surface with a 75-meter curve and a 75-meter straightaway.
Besides the $1 million prize to the winner, both Baily and Johnson will also take home a $500,000 appearance fee, making the total purse of the showdown race $2 million.
Bailey's statement did say he had made requests that the track be changed back to the original specifications and that the finish line be extended by 11 meters.
Bailey said his requests for changes "have all been denied by the race organisers who have been deficient in every aspect of this ambitious event."
